thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Service: /v1/generate (streaming). Severity: P1. p99 latency 2.8s (SLO 1.5s), p95 0.9s (SLO 0.5s). Streaming stalls reported (clients see chunks hang). Region: us-west-2. Possible hardware-level degradation. Paging: @oncall-ml @sre-ryan @infra-ingrid

oncall-ml: taking — joining now. any customer-facing impact known?

sre-ryan: ack. checking recent deploys and routing changes.

deploy-bot: no production deploys in last 60m. image tags unchanged.

infra-ingrid: looking at node pools — saw a tail in p99 specifically hitting nodes with GPU label inf=dedicated-gpu-usw2-12. grabbing node metrics now.

infra-ingrid: paste logs from node-gpu-12:
```
# nvidia-smi sample (last 5m)
temperature.gpu, utilization.gpu [%], ecc.errors.uncorrected
95, 10, 23
```

infra-ingrid: dmesg excerpt: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=10234 ... GPU falling off bus" and multiple thermal throttling events in last 10m. fan rpm spiked then stayed high.

oncall-ml: that ecc count is worrying. could explain corrupt frames leading to streaming stalls. do we have a pattern — same node(s) or rotating?

infra-ingrid: seems concentrated on node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-15 in the same rack. both show ECC uncorrected counts incrementing.

hw-jamie: on it — likely flaky GPU or power/thermal issue in that rack. I'll open a support incident with provider and request replacement / host reboot after we evacuate.

oncall-ml: quick mitigation proposals:
- drain node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-15 from serving pool
- apply routing fallback to model-small-quantized for streaming in us-west-2 to reduce heavy kernels
- enable cached-prefix for frequent prompts
- increase client-side chunk timeout to avoid immediate disconnects

infra-ingrid: running drain now. commands: 
```
kubectl taint nodes node-gpu-12 dedicated=throttle:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

infra-ingrid: drain started — pods are re-scheduling to other GPU nodes and to dedicated spare pool. routing control-plane switching to fallback model in 30s.

oncall-ml: rolling fallback route now: `traffic-rules apply --service=/v1/generate --region=us-west-2 --fallback=model-small-quantized --weight=100 --reason='mitigation for GPU throttle'`

sre-ryan: watch p99/p95 on dashboard. Also enabling short-circuit cache for repeating prefixes.

cs-zoe: noticed two external customers opened tickets about stalled streaming sessions: AcmeCorp (#2345) and BrightAds (#2346). I told them we are investigating and provided temporary workaround: use model-small-quantized or retry on reconnect.

infra-ingrid: after drain, node-gpu-12 shows GPU temperature dropping to 48C but ECC errors remain in kernel logs. provider ticket id: CLOUD-987654 opened. hardware team notified.

hw-jamie: provider response: scheduling host replacement window in 3h; suggested soft-reboot to clear transient faults but warned ECC counts persisted across reboots. Will push for hot-swap.

oncall-ml: current impact summary: about 4% of streaming requests in us-west-2 hit higher p99 and some client stalls. Dedicated customers on nodes got more exposure. We're switching those customers to reserved capacity in other racks or routing to multi-region fallback where allowed.

sre-ryan: p99 updated: 0.6s after routing change (measured at 1867504440). p95 back to 0.45s. still watching for errors as pods finish reschedule.

incident-bot: Reminder: set incident severity to MITIGATED when p99 < 1.5s for continuous 15m.

oncall-ml: agree. keep this P1 until hardware replacement or cleared ECC errors. will hand off to infra-ingrid for overnight monitoring in case hardware flaps.

infra-ingrid: I'll monitor rack and keep provider ticket open. adding alert rule to escalate if ECC uncorrected increases by >5 in 30m.

hw-jamie: action items: (1) confirm replacement, (2) collect core and GPU logs (nv-hostengine, dmesg, /var/log/messages), (3) validate node after replacement with burn-in test (cuda memtest).

cs-zoe: I'll email AcmeCorp and BrightAds with status and ticket links.

oncall-ml: handoff: wrapping up from my side. next oncall for infra is @infra-ingrid. if provider can't replace within SLA escalate to cloud-ops lead.

infra-ingrid: copying to #postmortems and will create incident ticket with timeline and mitigation steps. tagging for follow-up: @sre-ryan @hw-jamie @cs-zoe.

sre-ryan: thx all. quick notes for postmortem: root-cause hypothesis = GPU ECC uncorrected + thermal throttling in rack causing occasional compute faults and stalls -> triggers standalone client streaming stall and p99 tail. mitigation = drain, fallback routing, route dedicated customers off affected nodes, provider replacement.

oncall-ml: :thumbsup: closing my shift now; leave monitoring alerting window open.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied. p99 reduced to 0.6s at 1867504440. Incident status: mitigated -> awaiting hardware replacement.

infra-ingrid: handoff complete, monitoring for 2h. will post final resolution once host replaced.

hw-jamie: will follow up with provider ticket id CLOUD-987654 and post status here.

cs-zoe: tickets opened: SF-2345, SF-2346. customers notified.

oncall-ml: end of thread — follow-ups in postmortem doc and provider ticket.
